subject: maths
title: Primary 5 Angles: Straight Lines, Angles at a Point and Vertically Opposite Angles
seo_title: P5 Angles Worksheets: Free Primary 5 Maths Practice on Unknown Angles with Answers (MOE Syllabus)
standard_text: Angles on a straight line; angles at a point; vertically opposite angles; finding unknown angles
meta_desc: Free P5 angles practice: angles on a straight line (180°), at a point (360°), vertically opposite angles and unknown angles. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Angles on a straight line add up to 180°, angles at a point add up to 360°, and vertically opposite angles are equal.
key_sub: Example: on a straight line with 48° and 70°, the unknown angle is 180° − 48° − 70° = 62°.
body_html:
Three angle facts

To find an unknown angle, look for the fact that fits the figure. Add the angles you know, then subtract from the total.

Where the angles areAngle fact
On a straight lineThey add up to 180°
At a point (all the way round)They add up to 360°
Vertically opposite (two straight lines cross)They are equal
Next to each other where two lines crossThey add up to 180°

Worked examples

Straight line

Three angles on a straight line are 48°, 70° and ∠a. Find ∠a.

Straight line, so the total is 180°. 48° + 70° = 118°. 180° − 118° = 62°. Check: 48° + 70° + 62° = 180°.

Answer: 62°

At a point

Angles at a point are 200°, 95° and ∠b. Find ∠b.

At a point, so the total is 360°. 200° + 95° = 295°. 360° − 295° = 65°.

Answer: 65°

Named angles

AB and CD are straight lines that cross at O. ∠BOD = 70°. Find ∠AOC and ∠AOD.

∠AOC is vertically opposite ∠BOD, so ∠AOC = 70°. ∠AOD is on the straight line AB with ∠BOD: 180° − 70° = 110°.

Answer: ∠AOC = 70°, ∠AOD = 110°

Ratio of angles

∠a and ∠b are on a straight line. ∠a : ∠b = 2 : 3. Find ∠b.

Draw a model: ∠a is 2 units and ∠b is 3 units. 5 units = 180°, so 1 unit = 36°. ∠b = 3 × 36° = 108°.

Answer: 108°

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Using 360° for a straight line, or 180° at a pointStraight line: 180°. All the way round: 360°
Thinking two angles are equal because they look the sameAngles are equal only if a fact says so: vertically opposite, or marked equal. Then calculate
Taking angles next to each other as vertically oppositeVertically opposite angles are across the crossing point. Angles next to each other add up to 180°
Giving the total of the known angles as the answerAdd the known angles, then subtract the total from 180° or 360°

faq.q: What is taught about angles in P5 maths?
faq.a: Primary 5 students learn that angles on a straight line add up to 180°, angles at a point add up to 360° and vertically opposite angles are equal. They use these facts to find unknown angles in figures.

faq.q: How do I help my child find an unknown angle?
faq.a: Ask which fact fits the figure first: straight line (180°), at a point (360°) or vertically opposite (equal). Then add the known angles and subtract from the total, for example 180° − 48° − 70° = 62°.

faq.q: What is the most common mistake with angles?
faq.a: Using 360° for angles on a straight line, and thinking two angles are equal just because they look the same. Angles are equal only when a fact or a mark shows it, so always calculate.

faq.q: Is this in the MOE syllabus for Primary 5?
faq.a: Yes. Angles on a straight line, angles at a point and vertically opposite angles are in the Primary 5 Geometry content of the MOE 2021 Primary Mathematics Syllabus. Primary 6 builds on them in geometry questions for the PSLE.

items.q: The two angles marked m are equal. Find ∠m.
items.e: 180° − 70° = 110°. The two equal angles share it: 110° ÷ 2 = 55°.

items.q: Two angles are next to each other. One is 125° and the other is 65°. Can they make a straight line?
items.e: 125° + 65° = 190°. Angles on a straight line must add up to exactly 180°, so they cannot.

items.q: The angles are on a straight line. Find ∠g.
items.e: 25° + 95° = 120°. Angles on a straight line add up to 180°, so 180° − 120° = 60°.

items.q: A straight line is split into three angles. Two of them are 65° and 47°. Find the third angle.
items.e: 65° + 47° = 112°. 180° − 112° = 68°. (112° is the two angles added, not the unknown angle.)

items.q: Three equal angles together make a straight line. Find the size of each angle.
items.e: The three angles add up to 180°. 180° ÷ 3 = 60°. (120° comes from using 360°.)

items.q: Two angles are on a straight line. One is an acute angle of 38°. What is the other angle?
items.e: 180° − 38° = 142°. It is between 90° and 180°, so it is obtuse. (52° is 90° − 38°, which is for a right angle.)

items.q: AOB is a straight line. ∠AOC = 128°. Find ∠BOC.
items.e: ∠AOC and ∠BOC are on the straight line AOB, so they add up to 180°. ∠BOC = 180° − 128° = 52°.
The line is tilted, but it is still straight: 180° − 48° = 132°.

items.q: The angles are on a straight line. Find ∠h.
Two angles are on a straight line. One angle is 4 times as big as the other. Find the smaller angle.
items.e: The angles are 1 unit and 4 units: 5 units = 180°. 1 unit = 180° ÷ 5 = 36°. (The larger angle is 4 × 36° = 144°.)
Angles on a straight line add up to 180°. 180° − 115° = 65°. (360° − 115° = 245° is for angles at a point.)

items.q: Hafiz says ∠k = 50°, because it looks the same size as the 50° angle. Is he right?
items.e: Do not trust how an angle looks: work it out. 50° + 76° = 126°, and 180° − 126° = 54°.
Angles on a straight line add up to 180°. 180° − 40° = 140°.

items.q: The angles are on a straight line. Find ∠f.
items.e: First add the angles you know: 48° + 70° = 118°. Then subtract from 180°: 180° − 118° = 62°.

items.q: The angles are on a straight line. Find ∠e.
items.e: The small square shows a right angle: 90°. 90° + 35° = 125°, and 180° − 125° = 55°.

items.q: Two angles are on a straight line. One of them is 74°. Find the other angle.

items.e: Angles on a straight line add up to 180°. 180° − 73° = 107°.

items.q: The whole angle is a right angle. Find ∠n.
items.e: A right angle is 90°. 90° − 62° = 28°. (180° − 62° = 118° is for a straight line.)
The angles are on a straight line, so they add up to 180°, not 360°. 180° − 130° = 50°.

items.q: Angles on a straight line add up to …
items.e: A straight line makes a half turn: 180°. Two right angles make a straight line.

items.q: Five equal angles fit exactly around a point. Find the size of each angle.
Can angles of 150°, 120° and 100° fit around a point with no gaps or overlaps?
items.e: 150° + 120° + 100° = 370°. Angles at a point must add up to exactly 360°, so they would overlap by 10°.

items.q: Three angles are at a point. Two of them are 140° each. Find the third angle.
items.e: 140° + 140° = 280°. 360° − 280° = 80°. (220° comes from subtracting only one 140°.)

items.q: How many angles of 45° fit exactly around a point?
items.e: 360° ÷ 45° = 8. (4 is how many fit on a straight line: 180° ÷ 45° = 4.)

items.q: Four angles are at a point. One is a right angle and the other three are equal. Find the size of each of the three equal angles.
items.e: 360° − 90° = 270°. The three equal angles share it: 270° ÷ 3 = 90°.
The small square is 90°. 90° + 125° + 60° = 275°, and 360° − 275° = 85°. (175° comes from forgetting the right angle.)

items.q: Angles at a point add up to …
items.e: Angles at a point make a complete turn: 360°.
360° − 100° = 260°. The two equal angles share it: 260° ÷ 2 = 130°.
360° − 120° = 240°. ∠p is 1 unit and ∠q is 2 units: 3 units = 240°, so 1 unit = 80°. (120° comes from treating the two angles as equal.)
Angles at a point add up to 360°. 360° − 130° = 230°. (50° comes from using 180°, and 490° from adding.)

items.q: Four angles are at a point. Three of them are 95°, 120° and 85°. Find the fourth angle.
Three angles at a point are in the ratio 2 : 3 : 4. Find the largest angle.
items.e: 2 + 3 + 4 = 9 units = 360°. 1 unit = 360° ÷ 9 = 40°. The largest angle is 4 units: 4 × 40° = 160°. (80° comes from using 180°.)
Angles at a point add up to 360°. 110° + 135° = 245°, and 360° − 245° = 115°.
Angles at a point add up to 360°. 360° ÷ 3 = 120°. (180° ÷ 3 = 60° is for a straight line.)
Add the angles you know, then subtract from 360°: 360° − 250° = 110°. 250° is the total of the two angles, not the unknown angle.
One angle is a reflex angle. 200° + 95° = 295°, and 360° − 295° = 65°.

items.q: A reflex angle of 250° and one other angle make a complete turn. Find the other angle.
items.e: A complete turn is 360°. 360° − 250° = 110°. (70° comes from 250° − 180°, and 610° from adding.)

items.q: Two angles are at a point. One is 5 times as big as the other. Find the larger angle.
items.e: 1 unit + 5 units = 6 units = 360°. 1 unit = 60°, so the larger angle is 5 × 60° = 300° (a reflex angle). (150° comes from using 180°.)
∠k is next to 86° on a straight line, not opposite it. 180° − 86° = 94°. Angles can look equal and still be different, so use the angle facts.

items.q: Two straight lines cross. One angle is 27°. Find the angle vertically opposite it.
items.e: Vertically opposite angles are equal, so it is also 27°. (153° is the angle next to it.)

items.q: AB and CD are straight lines that cross at O. ∠AOC = 70°. Find ∠BOD.
items.e: ∠BOD and ∠AOC are vertically opposite, so they are equal: ∠BOD = 70°.

items.q: AB and CD are straight lines that cross at O. ∠AOD = 132°. Find ∠AOC.
items.e: ∠AOC is next to ∠AOD on the straight line CD, so they add up to 180°: 180° − 132° = 48°. (∠AOC is not vertically opposite ∠AOD. ∠BOC is.)

items.q: Two straight lines cross. Find ∠b.
items.e: ∠b is vertically opposite the 65° angle. Vertically opposite angles are equal, so ∠b = 65°.
∠s and 105° are on a straight line: 180° − 105° = 75°. ∠t is vertically opposite 105°, so it is 105°. ∠u is vertically opposite ∠s: 75°.
∠d is vertically opposite the 145° angle. Vertically opposite angles are equal, so ∠d = 145°.
Vertically opposite angles are across the crossing point from each other: ∠a and ∠c (also ∠b and ∠d). Angles next to each other, like ∠a and ∠b, add up to 180°.

items.q: Two straight lines cross. Two vertically opposite angles add up to 100°. Find the size of each of the other two angles.
items.e: The two equal opposite angles are 100° ÷ 2 = 50° each. The angles next to them are 180° − 50° = 130°.
∠m and 146° are next to each other on a straight line, so they add up to 180°. 180° − 146° = 34°. (They are not vertically opposite.)

items.q: Arjun says that vertically opposite angles add up to 180°. Is he right?
c: Yes, they are on a straight line
items.e: Vertically opposite angles are equal. It is the angles next to each other (on a straight line) that add up to 180°.

items.q: Two straight lines cross. Find ∠c.
items.e: ∠c is vertically opposite the 72° angle. Vertically opposite angles are equal, so ∠c = 72°.

items.q: Three straight lines meet at a point. Find ∠w.
items.e: ∠w is vertically opposite the 80° angle, so it is also 80°.
∠h and 75° are next to each other on a straight line, so they add up to 180°. 180° − 75° = 105°. (They are not vertically opposite.)
∠p is on a straight line with 64°: 180° − 64° = 116°. ∠q is vertically opposite 64°, so it is 64°. ∠r is vertically opposite ∠p, so it is 116°.

items.q: Two straight lines cross. Find ∠a.
items.e: ∠a is vertically opposite the 40° angle. Vertically opposite angles are equal, so ∠a = 40°.
∠g and 130° are next to each other on a straight line, so they add up to 180°. 180° − 130° = 50°. (They are not vertically opposite.)
∠e is vertically opposite the 155° angle. Vertically opposite angles are equal, so ∠e = 155°.
∠f and 58° are next to each other on a straight line, so they add up to 180°. 180° − 58° = 122°. (They are not vertically opposite.)

items.q: Two straight lines cross. One of the angles is a right angle. What are the other three angles?
items.e: The angle next to 90° is 180° − 90° = 90°, and vertically opposite angles are equal. So all four angles are 90°.

items.q: The angles are on a straight line. Find ∠t.

items.e: ∠u is on a straight line with 128°: 180° − 128° = 52°. ∠v is vertically opposite 128°, so ∠v = 128°.
The square is 90°. 90° + 150° = 240°. 360° − 240° = 120°, and 120° ÷ 2 = 60°. (105° comes from forgetting the right angle.)

items.q: Three straight lines meet at a point. Which angle is vertically opposite ∠b?
items.e: Follow the two lines that make ∠b through the crossing point. The angle between them on the other side is ∠e.
The 70° angle and ∠x are on the straight line below it: 180° − 70° = 110°. The 50° angle does not help here.

items.q: AB and CD are straight lines that cross at O. ∠BOC = 50° and ∠BOE = 60°. Find ∠DOE.
items.e: Step 1: ∠BOD is next to ∠BOC on the straight line CD: 180° − 50° = 130°. Step 2: ∠DOE = ∠BOD − ∠BOE = 130° − 60° = 70°.

items.q: Three straight lines meet at a point. Find ∠b.
items.e: Step 1: the angle between 40° and 65° on the straight line is 180° − 40° − 65° = 75°. Step 2: ∠b is vertically opposite it, so ∠b = 75°.

items.q: Three straight lines meet at a point. Find ∠c.
items.e: The angle between 55° and ∠c is vertically opposite 65°, so it is 65°. Then on the straight line: 180° − 55° − 65° = 60°.
∠p: 180° − 50° − 60° = 70° (straight line). ∠q is vertically opposite 50°, and ∠r is vertically opposite 60°.

items.q: Two straight lines cross, and one more line starts at the crossing point. Find ∠e.
items.e: Step 1: on the straight line, the angle at the right is 180° − 55° − 55° = 70°. Step 2: ∠e is vertically opposite it, so ∠e = 70°.

items.q: Three straight lines meet at a point. Find ∠a.
items.e: The three angles above the flat line are on a straight line. 40° + 75° = 115°, and 180° − 115° = 65°.
The two angles are next to each other on a straight line: 2 × ∠h = 180°, so ∠h = 90°. (45° comes from 180° ÷ 4, and 60° from 180° ÷ 3.)

items.q: Three straight lines cross at one point and make six equal angles. Find ∠w.
items.e: Angles at a point add up to 360°. 360° ÷ 6 = 60°. (30° comes from 180° ÷ 6.)

items.q: The angles are on a straight line. Find ∠y.
Two straight lines cross, and one more line starts at the crossing point. Find ∠d.
items.e: The three angles above the flat line are on a straight line. 70° + 55° = 125°, and 180° − 125° = 55°.

items.q: Two straight lines cross, and one more line starts at the crossing point. Find ∠m.
items.e: Step 1: next to 65° on the straight line is 180° − 65° = 115°. Step 2: the angle below, between the sloping line and the flat line, is vertically opposite it, so it is 115°. Step 3: ∠m = 115° − 70° = 45°.

items.q: Two straight lines cross at right angles. One more line starts at the crossing point. Find ∠f.
items.e: The lines cross at right angles, so all four angles they make are 90°. So ∠f + 50° = 90°, and ∠f = 90° − 50° = 40°.

items.q: Kavya says ∠n = 60°, because all three angles look equal. Is she right?
items.e: 61° + 60° = 121°, and 180° − 121° = 59°. The angles look almost the same, but they are not equal.

sets.title: Multi-step and word problems: equal angles and ratio

items.q: Farah opens a paper fan until its two outer edges make a straight line. The fan has 6 equal sections. Find the angle of each section.
items.e: The sections share a straight angle: 180° ÷ 6 = 30°. (60° comes from using 360°.)

items.q: Two straight paths at East Coast Park cross. One of the four angles is 58°. Find the sum of the other three angles.
items.e: The four angles are at a point, so they add up to 360°. 360° − 58° = 302°. Check: 122° + 58° + 122° = 302°.

items.q: ∠m and ∠n are on a straight line. ∠m is 40° more than ∠n. Find ∠m.
items.e: Take away the extra 40°: 180° − 40° = 140°. That is 2 equal units, so 1 unit = 70°. ∠m = 70° + 40° = 110°. (90° comes from making the angles equal; 200° from using 360°.)

items.q: A pair of scissors is like two straight lines crossing at the screw. The handles are opened to an angle of 35°. Find the angle between the blades.
items.e: The angle between the blades is vertically opposite the angle between the handles, so it is equal: 35°.

items.q: Two straight lines cross. A third line splits one angle into two equal angles. Find ∠k.
items.e: Next to 64° on the straight line: 180° − 64° = 116°. The two equal angles share it: 116° ÷ 2 = 58°. (148° comes from using 360°.)

items.q: Mei Ling faces north. She turns clockwise until she faces south-east. Find the angle she turns through.
items.e: North to east is a right angle (90°). East to south-east is half a right angle (45°). 90° + 45° = 135°.

items.q: A bicycle wheel has 10 spokes spaced equally around the centre. Find the angle between two spokes next to each other.
items.e: The spokes share a complete turn: 360° ÷ 10 = 36°. (18° comes from using 180°.)

items.q: Two straight roads cross at a junction. One angle between them is 72°. Find the sum of the two obtuse angles.
items.e: Each obtuse angle is 180° − 72° = 108°. The two obtuse angles are vertically opposite, so they are equal: 108° + 108° = 216°.

items.q: A ladder stands on a flat floor and leans against a wall. The angle between the ladder and the floor on the wall side is 68°. Find the angle between the ladder and the floor on the other side.
items.e: The two angles are on the straight floor, so they add up to 180°. 180° − 68° = 112°.

items.q: ∠p, ∠q and ∠r are at a point. ∠p : ∠q : ∠r = 3 : 4 : 5. Find ∠r.

items.e: ∠e is 1 unit and ∠f is 3 units: 4 units = 180°, so 1 unit = 45°. ∠f = 3 × 45° = 135°. (60° comes from 180° ÷ 3.)

items.q: The ceiling fan in an HDB flat has 3 blades spaced equally around the centre. Find the angle between two blades next to each other.
items.e: The blades share a complete turn: 360° ÷ 3 = 120°. (60° comes from using 180°.)

items.q: ∠a and ∠b are on a straight line. ∠a : ∠b = 2 : 3. Find ∠b.
∠c and ∠d are on a straight line. ∠c : ∠d = 1 : 5. How much bigger is ∠d than ∠c?
items.e: 6 units = 180°, so 1 unit = 30°. ∠d is 4 units more than ∠c: 4 × 30° = 120°. (150° is ∠d itself; 240° comes from using 360°.)
118° + 120° = 238°, and 360° − 238° = 122°. Angles that look equal are not always equal: calculate.

items.q: AOB is a straight line. ∠AOC = ∠COD and ∠BOD = 40°. Find ∠AOC.
items.e: 180° − 40° = 140°. ∠AOC and ∠COD are equal, so each is 140° ÷ 2 = 70°. (160° comes from using 360°.)

items.q: The angles are on a straight line. Angles with the same mark are equal. Find ∠h.
items.e: The two angles with one dash are 35° each: 35° + 35° = 70°. 180° − 70° = 110°. The two angles with two dashes share it: 110° ÷ 2 = 55°. (90° comes from 180° ÷ 2, which leaves out the 35° angles.)
360° − 105° = 255°. The three equal angles share it: 255° ÷ 3 = 85°. (90° comes from 360° ÷ 4; the four angles are not all equal. 25° comes from using 180°.)

items.q: The legs of a folding chair at a void deck event cross like an X. The angle between the legs at the top is 50°. Find the angle between the legs at the side of the X.
items.e: The side angle is next to the 50° angle on a straight leg, so it is 180° − 50° = 130°. (50° is the vertically opposite angle at the bottom.)

items.q: Mdm Wong cuts a round pandan cake into 8 equal slices. Every cut goes through the centre. Zhi Hao eats 3 slices. Find the angle at the centre made by the slices that are left.
items.e: Each slice is 360° ÷ 8 = 45°. 5 slices are left: 5 × 45° = 225°. (135° is the 3 slices that were eaten.)
